basis: Werner’s Q1 2024 earnings release was the earliest qualifying disclosure found. Its consolidated GAAP income statement reports operating revenue of $769,080,000 for the three months ended March 31, 2024, versus $832,714,000 a year earlier. That was a 7.64% decline and $21,998,300 below the $791,078,300 threshold. Both figures include fuel surcharges and reflect intersegment eliminations.

coverage.detail: November 1, 2023, Q3 release. Updated guidance covered the 2023 truck count, capital spending and truckload operating metrics. The One-Way revenue-per-mile outlook applied to Q4 2023. The release gave no Q1 2024 consolidated revenue range.
On the November 1 call, management anticipated lower capital spending in the first half of 2024. Its numerical fleet guidance covered full-year 2023. Neither established Q1 2024 revenue.

At Stephens on November 14, management described more than $3.3 billion of consolidated revenue over the trailing twelve months and discussed the 2024 bid season. It gave no Q1 consolidated revenue bound.

February 6, 2024, Q4 release. The headline 5% revenue decline was the Q4 2023 actual. Forward guidance called for a 3%–6% decline in first-half One-Way Truckload revenue per total mile excluding fuel surcharges, and 0%–3% annual growth in Dedicated revenue per truck per week. Neither measure bounded consolidated Q1 revenue.
The February 6 investor presentation confirms the One-Way comparison was first-half 2024 versus first-half 2023. Its guidance table contains no Q1 consolidated sales forecast.

On the February 6 call, the CEO discussed the usual sequential Q1 pressure from weather and lower post-holiday shipping volumes in response to a trucking-margin question. He gave no numerical upper bound for Q1 consolidated revenue.
At Stifel on February 13, management discussed Q4 peak volumes and the possibility of Logistics approaching $1 billion for the year. Neither figure established quarterly consolidated revenue.

At Citi on February 21, management reiterated the annual TTS fleet outlook of down 3% to flat. Its discussion of a roughly 30% historical sequential Q4-to-Q1 decline concerned earnings seasonality. It gave no consolidated Q1 sales ceiling.
The February 5 conference notice identified public webcasts for Stifel and Citi and listed the February 22 Barclays event as investor meetings. The notice contained no Q1 revenue update.
The February 15 Form 8-K disclosed executive salaries and equity awards.
The March 1 Form 8-K concerned a director’s departure.
The March 7 amendment concerned correspondence about the same director’s resignation. Neither March filing supplied a revenue update.
The March 28 notice scheduled Q1 results for April 30 after market close. Its $3.3 billion revenue reference described full-year 2023. It gave no preliminary Q1 figure.
Werner’s event record confirms it publicly released first-quarter earnings on April 30 after market close and held its call that day at 4:00 p.m. Central.

publication_date_evidence: Exhibit 99.1 carries an April 30, 2024 Omaha dateline and announces results for the quarter ended March 31. Werner’s IR event record independently confirms the April 30 after-close release, before the May 9 Form 10-Q filing.
